what: United Microelectronics is a Taiwanese contract chipmaker. It manufactures chips designed by other companies, focusing on mature process nodes rather than the leading edge: the chips used in displays, power management, connectivity and cars.
customers: Fabless chip designers, consumer electronics companies, carmakers and industrial customers worldwide.
money: wafer manufacturing on mature and specialty process nodes
moat: Depreciated factories running mature processes at low cost, where customers qualify a design once and keep producing it for years.
risks: Chinese foundries are adding mature-node capacity and pushing prices down
Consumer electronics demand has been weak
Revenue has fallen about 3% a year over three years
opportunities: Cash of about $5 billion exceeds its debt
A dividend yield near 3%, unusual for a chipmaker
Specialty processes for displays and power management are less exposed to price competition than plain logic
watch: Factory utilisation and average selling price per wafer.
